blogPosts.title: How Much Does a Home Extension Cost in Southbank in 2026?
blogPosts.excerpt: A detailed cost breakdown for home extensions in Southbank, including permits, materials, and labour. Average prices from $4,000 per square metre.
body: Planning a home extension in Southbank in 2026? Costs have shifted with material prices and labour demand. Expect to pay between $4,000 and $6,500 per square metre for a single-storey extension, depending on finish quality. Two-storey additions can push that to $7,000 per square metre due to structural requirements. Always factor in site conditions — Southbank's clay soil often requires deeper footings, adding $10,000–$20,000 to the budget.

Council permits in Melbourne's inner suburbs like Southbank take 8-12 weeks. You'll need a building permit, and possibly a planning permit if you're altering the building envelope. UGL handles all permit applications for you. We've been navigating Southbank's council requirements since 1899, so we know exactly what's needed. Don't forget to budget for extra costs like temporary accommodation ($3,000–$8,000) if your extension is substantial.

Material costs vary widely. Structural steel has risen 15% in 2025, while timber remains stable. Concrete prices in Melbourne are around $300 per cubic metre delivered. For a 30-square-metre extension, expect concrete costs of $6,000–$9,000. Timber framing adds another $8,000–$12,000. To save money, consider exposed aggregate concrete floors — they look modern and reduce tiling costs. UGL can advise on the best materials for your Southbank home.

Labour is the biggest cost driver in Southbank. Carpenters charge $70–$90 per hour, electricians $90–$120, and plumbers $80–$110. A typical extension takes 12-16 weeks with a team of 4-6 trades. To keep costs down, book your trades early — demand spikes during Melbourne's spring building season. Fixed-price contracts, like those UGL offers, protect you from price rises. We lock in rates at signing, so you won't pay more if material prices jump.

Hidden costs can trip up homeowners. Unexpected site conditions — like old asbestos in a 1970s Southbank home — can add $5,000–$15,000 for removal. Underground services relocation (water, sewer, gas) may cost $3,000–$8,000. Always include a 15-20% contingency in your budget. UGL's process includes a comprehensive site inspection before quoting, so we catch these issues early and include them in your fixed price.

To save money on your Southbank extension, consider a design-and-build approach. It cuts out the architect's separate fees (usually 8-15% of build cost). Open-plan layouts reduce wall framing and plumbing runs, saving 5-10% compared to segmented rooms. And choose standard finishes — custom joinery and feature tiles look great but blow the budget. UGL offers free initial consultations to walk through your options and give you a realistic cost estimate before you commit.

Financing your extension? Many homeowners in Southbank use construction loans or equity release. Talk to a broker who understands building projects. UGL works with several local lenders who offer competitive rates for renovations. We can provide detailed cost breakdowns to support your loan application. The average Southbank homeowner recoups 70-80% of extension costs in added property value — so it's a solid investment if you plan to sell within 5-10 years.

Ready to start your Southbank extension? Call UGL on +61 3 8413 3300 for a free on-site consultation. We'll measure up, discuss your wishlist, and provide a written fixed-price quote within a week. With 126 years of building experience, you're in safe hands. Don't let rising costs scare you — book early, budget smartly, and enjoy your new space by the end of 2026.

blogPosts.title: Commercial Fitout Costs in Melbourne CBD: 2026 Guide
blogPosts.excerpt: A complete guide to commercial fitout costs in Melbourne's CBD, including per-square-metre rates, approvals and timelines for offices and retail.
body: Fitting out a commercial space in Melbourne CBD in 2026? Costs range from $1,500 to $4,000 per square metre depending on the level of fitout. A basic 'category A' fitout (floor coverings, mechanical, electrical, fire) starts around $1,500 per square metre. A full 'category B' fitout with partitions, joinery, finishes, and furniture can reach $4,000 or more. UGL's commercial team has completed dozens of CBD fitouts and knows how to deliver value without compromising quality.

Location matters in Melbourne's CBD. Heritage-listed buildings in the CBD's east require special approvals and may limit changes to facades and internal structures. Newer towers in Docklands offer more flexibility but have higher tenant amenities fees. Always check the building's mechanical and electrical capacity before signing a lease — upgrading these in a high-rise can add $200–$500 per square metre to your fitout budget.

Permits for commercial fitouts in Melbourne City Council take 4-8 weeks for standard works. You'll need a building permit, and if you're changing the use class (e.g., retail to office), a planning permit as well. Fire services, disabled access, and egress must comply with the Building Code of Australia (BCA). UGL engages accredited building surveyors early to streamline approvals. Our in-house engineers handle structural and fire safety reports, saving you weeks of delays.

Labour costs in the CBD are higher than suburban areas. Electricians charge $100–$140 per hour, plasterers $60–$80, and carpenters $80–$100. Because CBD sites have restricted access hours (often only 7am-6pm weekdays, and no weekend work in some buildings), you may need to pay overtime. To minimise disruption, UGL often works overnight or in stages, which costs more but can halve project duration. Plan for 8-16 weeks total for a typical 200-square-metre fitout.

Materials and finishes are where you can control costs. Standard plasterboard partitions, laminate benchtops, and carpet tiles keep budgets low. Want a premium look? Glass partitions, stone benchtops, and timber floors add $500–$1,000 per square metre. LED lighting is mandatory in new commercial builds, but smart controls can save on energy bills long-term. UGL's procurement team sources materials at competitive trade prices and passes those savings to you.

Don't forget the soft costs: design fees (5-10% of build cost), permits ($5,000–$15,000), building surveyor fees ($2,000–$5,000), and contingency (10-15%). Your furniture, IT, and audio-visual fitout may cost an additional $500–$1,000 per square metre. UGL offers turnkey packages that include everything from design to handover, so you have one point of contact and no surprises. Our fixed-price contracts cover all known costs upfront.

Timing is everything. The best time to fit out in Melbourne CBD is between March and May or September and November, when trade availability is highest. Avoid December to February (Christmas shutdowns and heat waves) and June to August (winter rains can slow external works). UGL's project managers coordinate with building management, lift carriers, and cleaners to keep the schedule on track. We've delivered fitouts in as little as 6 weeks for urgent projects.

Ready to fit out your Melbourne CBD space? Contact UGL's commercial team on +61 3 8413 3300 for a free consultation and written quote. We'll visit your site, understand your brand and operational needs, and provide a transparent cost breakdown. With 126 years of building experience, UGL is your partner for a smooth, on-budget fitout in 2026.

blogPosts.title: Exposed Aggregate Concrete Driveways: Cost & Design in Melbourne
blogPosts.excerpt: Everything you need to know about exposed aggregate driveways in Melbourne — costs, designs, sealing and local contractors. Prices from $75 per square metre.
body: Exposed aggregate concrete driveways are a popular choice for Melbourne homes. They offer a non-slip surface that's durable and looks great. In 2026, expect to pay $75–$120 per square metre for a standard exposed aggregate driveway, including removal of old concrete. Higher-end mixes with coloured aggregates and decorative borders can cost $130–$180 per square metre. UGL's concrete team has installed hundreds of driveways across Southbank and inner Melbourne.

The cost depends on the aggregate you choose. Local river pebbles are cheapest at $50–$70 per tonne. Decorative aggregates like quartz, granite, or recycled glass cost $100–$250 per tonne. Colour washing the concrete base adds $10–$20 per square metre. For a typical two-car driveway (40 square metres), total cost ranges from $3,000 to $7,200. UGL provides a detailed quote after measuring your site and discussing your design preferences.

Melbourne's climate is perfect for exposed aggregate — the surface stays cool in summer and drains well in rain. But you need good site preparation. Most Melbourne soils are reactive clay, which requires a compacted base of 150mm of crushed rock and steel mesh reinforcement. Without proper subgrade preparation, your driveway can crack within a few years. UGL always does a soil test and recommends thickness based on traffic load (100mm for cars, 150mm for heavy vehicles).

Design options are endless. You can choose a single colour or two-tone patterns. Exposed aggregate works well with stone edging, asphalt, or brick borders. Stencilled patterns (like herringbone or cobblestone) add $20–$40 per square metre. For a modern look, consider a charcoal or grey base with white quartz aggregate. UGL's design team can help you choose a combination that complements your Melbourne home's facade and landscaping.

Sealing is essential for longevity. A quality penetrating sealer applied after curing (28 days) costs $5–$10 per square metre and protects against stains and weathering. Reseal every 2-3 years. Unsealed driveways may discolour from oil spills or Melbourne's pollution. UGL includes sealing in our driveway packages and offers maintenance reminders. We also suggest a light broom finish or exposed aggregate surface to improve slip resistance — important in Melbourne's wet winters.

Permits are usually not required for driveways unless you're altering the crossover (the kerb ramp). If your Melbourne home is in a heritage overlay, you may need a planning permit. UGL checks all local council rules before starting work. We also handle drainage — driveway runoff must not flow onto neighbouring properties or into stormwater drains without approval. Our team installs channels or soakwells as needed, compliant with Melbourne Water requirements.

Timing: concrete work in Melbourne is best done in spring or autumn (October-November or March-April). Avoid summer heat (above 30°C) which causes rapid curing and cracking, and winter rain (June-August) which delays excavation. UGL schedules your driveway installation around weather forecasts. A typical driveway takes 3-5 days from demolition to completion, including curing time of 24-48 hours before you can walk on it, and 7 days before parking.

Ready for a new driveway? Call UGL's concrete team on +61 3 8413 3300 for a free quote. We'll discuss aggregates, colours, and sealing options that suit your Southbank or Melbourne home. With 126 years of experience, your driveway will look great and last for decades. Book now — our calendar fills up fast in the building season.

blogPosts.title: Rail Infrastructure Projects in Victoria: What to Expect in 2026
blogPosts.excerpt: An overview of major rail infrastructure projects in Victoria for 2026, including level crossing removals, new stations, and rolling stock upgrades. UGL's role and opportunities.
body: Victoria's rail infrastructure boom continues in 2026 with several major projects underway. The Level Crossing Removal Project (LXRP) is removing 110 crossings by 2030, with 20+ scheduled for 2026. New stations at sites like Ardeer and Glenroy will include modern facilities, park-and-ride, and solar panels. UGL is a key contractor on LXRP, delivering track work, signalling upgrades, and station builds. Our team of 400+ rail specialists is based right here in Southbank.

The Metro Tunnel is entering its final commissioning phase in 2026, transforming the CBD rail network. Five new underground stations at Arden, Parkville, Anzac Station, and two at Town Hall will open in 2025-26. UGL has been involved in track laying, power supply, and systems integration. For subcontractors, there are opportunities in finishes, fire services, and mechanical works. UGL regularly partners with local Victorian SMEs for these projects.

Rolling stock is another huge area. The X'Trapolis 2.0 trains (65 x 7-car trainsets) are being built at UGL's Newport facility, creating 750 jobs. In 2026, the first trains will begin testing on the Craigieburn and Sunbury lines. UGL is also maintaining the VLocity fleet and the E-Class trams for Yarra Trams. If you're a railway engineer or technician, UGL is hiring in electrical, mechanical, and project management roles — check our careers page.

Regional rail upgrades are also active. The Shepparton Line Upgrade (duplication and signalling) and the Warrnambool Line (speed improvements) are ongoing. UGL is delivering track formation and level crossing works in regional Victoria. These projects require careful logistics — materials are transported from our Southbank depot to site daily. We prioritise local employment, with 90% of our regional workforce drawn from the local area.

Signalling and communications are the backbone of modern rail. The High Capacity Signalling Project (digital signalling) will roll out on the Sunbury line in 2026, enabling automatic train operation. UGL's engineering team designs and installs signalling systems including axle counters, train stops, and control centres. This is highly specialised work requiring accredited engineers. If you're considering a career in rail signalling, UGL offers apprenticeships and graduate programs.

Safety compliance is non-negotiable. All rail infrastructure work in Victoria must follow the Rail Safety National Law and the MTM (Metro Trains Melbourne) Network Rules. UGL holds AS 4801 (safety) and ISO 9001 certification. Every site has a dedicated safety manager, and all workers undergo induction to the relevant rail corridor. We maintain a zero-harm culture — in 2025, we recorded over 1 million hours without a lost-time injury across our rail projects.

To win rail work in Victoria, you need to be pre-qualified through the VicTrack or LXRP supplier panels. UGL can mentor smaller contractors through the process. Subcontractors in concreting, steel fixing, electrical, and civil works are always in demand. We pay competitive rates and provide long-term contracts. Contact UGL's supply chain team to register your interest for 2026 projects.

Want to work on Victoria's rail future? UGL is recruiting now for 2026. Visit our careers page or call +61 3 8413 3300. From apprenticeships to senior engineering roles, we're building the next generation of rail infrastructure — right here in Southbank and across the state.
